primary_topics: Wedding anniversary toast by CJP at the 50th anniversary celebration of Ave and Helen Cruz, May 22, 2015 -- at what appears to be a San Beda Law Alumni Association event

CJP's lifelong Bedan aspiration: intercepted en route to San Beda enrollment by Dean Salonga at FEU; honorary Bedan membership proclaimed by Ave; dream for San Beda to have its own native Chief Justice

Ave Cruz's career arc: youngest bar topnotcher at 20, LLM at Michigan at 24, Mobil general counsel at 28, ACCRA founding partner at 31 -- and his parallel musical career (hymns for ACCRA, San Beda, ALA; love songs for Helen)
The missed Chief Justice opportunity: Ave declined Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986; had he accepted, there would have been no CJs Davide, Panganiban or Puno

CJP's Bedan aspiration: at Mapa High (opposite San Beda in Mendiola) for over 60 years; was heading to San Beda to enroll in law from Cataluna Street, Sampaloc; intercepted in front of FEU by Dean Jovito R. Salonga who 'led me in'
Honorary Bedan: proclaimed by Ave during a San Beda Law Alumni reunion when CJP was Chief Justice; 'chosen by roaring acclamation, not by quiet balloting'

San Beda's missing CJ: several bar topnotchers (including the current one, the youngest, and Justice Florenz Regalado who had the highest grade in history) but never a Chief Justice -- 'Actually that is the fault of Ave'
Ave's legal career milestones: youngest bar topnotcher in history at 20; LLM University of Michigan at 24; general counsel of Mobil Philippines at 28; founding partner of ACCRA Law at 31

Ave's musical parallel: wanted to be a music composer and master pianist like his father; mother ordered him to take up law; but composed hymns of ACCRA, San Beda College and ALA, plus love songs to win Helen Canave's reluctant heart

The Deputy Prime Minister miscalculation: declined Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986 to stay with PM Salvador Laurel as Deputy PM; short-lived when the 1987 Constitution abolished the positions; had he joined the SC in 1986, he would have become CJ after Narvasa retired in 1998; would have reigned until age 70 (December 17, 2010) -- 'there would have been no Chief Justices Hilario Davide Jr., Artemio V. Panganiban and Reynato S. Puno'

CJP's thanksgiving to Ave: 'in thanksgiving for giving me the chance to lead our judiciary, I campaigned robustly for him to become President of the Asean Law Association, which he attained last February'; as ALA President, 'he now lords over six Asean Chief Justices who are his vice presidents'

Greatest achievement: 'his greatest achievement is not in law, or in music, or in public service. Not even in ALA. In my humble opinion, his greatest achievement is convincing Helen to become his wife 50 years ago, and persuading her to repeat her sweet Yes annually during the last 50 years'

Toast and cheeky wish: 'May they have another 50 years of blessed togetherness. And may they celebrate tonight by adding a new member of the Cruz family who will greet the world nine months from now.'

stances.claim: Had Ave Cruz accepted Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986, he would have become Chief Justice after Narvasa's 1998 retirement and reigned until 2010 -- meaning there would have been no Chief Justices Davide, Panganiban or Puno. CJP explicitly names himself as one of the three who would not have been CJ, making this a rare autobiographical counterfactual that acknowledges the contingency of his own judicial career.
stances.rhetorical_move: counterfactual-gratitude: the three non-existent CJs as the debt owed to Ave's choice -- and the basis for CJP's campaign to make Ave ALA President

stances.claim: Ave Cruz's greatest achievement is not law, music, public service, or even ALA -- it is 'convincing Helen to become his wife 50 years ago, and persuading her to repeat her sweet Yes annually during the last 50 years.' This is CJP's highest category of achievement: the personal and relational, above all professional accomplishments.
stances.rhetorical_move: hierarchy-of-achievements inversion: the personal triumph (winning Helen's annual Yes) ranked above the professional (ALA, law career, music)

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered May 22, 2015 at the 50th Wedding Anniversary of Ave and Helen Cruz, this toast by CJP opens with a Shakespeare-styled salutation ('Friends, Bedans and Countrymen, please lend me your ears') and an affectionate roast of Senate President Franklin Drilon ('not a Bedan -- finished only from the second best law school in the country'). CJP recalls his lifelong Bedan aspiration: headed from Cataluna Street to San Beda to enroll in law, but 'intercepted when already in front of FEU by Dean Jovito R. Salonga who led me in'; his dream fulfilled only when Ave proclaimed him honorary member 'by roaring acclamation, not by quiet balloting.' He tracks Ave's career arc: youngest bar topnotcher in history at 20; LLM at Michigan at 24; Mobil general counsel at 28; ACCRA founding partner at 31 -- alongside his musical parallel (composer of ACCRA, San Beda and ALA hymns, plus 'passionate love songs to win the reluctant heart of Helen Canave'). The critical counterfactual: had Ave accepted Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986 instead of serving as Deputy PM under Laurel (abolished by the 1987 Constitution), he would have become Chief Justice after Narvasa's 1998 retirement and reigned until 2010 -- 'there would have been no Chief Justices Hilario Davide Jr., Artemio V. Panganiban and Reynato S. Puno.' In thanksgiving for this inadvertent gift, CJP campaigned for Ave to become ALA President (attained February 2015); 'he now lords over six Asean Chief Justices who are his vice presidents.' But the supreme tribute: 'his greatest achievement is not in law, or in music, or in public service. Not even in ALA. In my humble opinion, his greatest achievement is convincing Helen to become his wife 50 years ago, and persuading her to repeat her sweet Yes annually during the last 50 years.' Closes with a toast and cheeky wish for another 50 years -- 'and may they celebrate tonight by adding a new member of the Cruz family who will greet the world nine months from now.'
